## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by flattened cells joined end-to-end into long, often slightly twisted filaments surrounded by a gelatinous sheath. Desmidium baileyi typically has deeply constricted cells with rounded or lobed margins, giving the filament a distinctive beaded or scalloped appearance. It occurs in freshwater habitats such as ponds, marshes, bogs, and other still or slow-moving waters, particularly among aquatic vegetation. Like other desmids, it contributes to primary production and forms part of the microscopic food web in freshwater ecosystems.
